endorsements.quote: Form a Multidisciplinary Oversight Board (MOB) with at least: o A clinical psychologist or psychiatrist o An XR/AI systems developer o A bioethicist o A legal/data privacy expert o A patient or caregiver representative MOB responsibilities include: o Approving mitigation strategies and deployment plans o Reviewing incident reports and adverse events o Conducting quarterly reviews of equity impacts, content updates, and data safety audits

Meeting frequency and triggers include initial approval review before first deployment of any therapeutic module, quarterly oversight meetings to review performance metrics, system logs, and user feedback, and ad hoc reviews triggered by major algorithm or software updates, flagged adverse events, and significant requests from patients or therapists.

Additionally, the MOB vets software updates and data pipeline changes for legal and ethical alignment [ 33 ], engages in scenario modeling to anticipate emergent ethical-legal conflicts [ 26 ], and publishes transparent, de-identified reports to maintain public trust.
Publish brief, de-identified oversight summaries to bolster trust and invite external feedback.
All decisions and audits should be recorded in a secure compliance system, with summaries released publicly to promote ethical transparency [ 23 ].

To ensure ethical and legal compliance, institutions adopting immersive AI therapy must map the protocol to jurisdiction-specific requirements, implement layered consent aligned with GDPR and CCPA, submit SaMD tools for premarket review when required, and build traceability and explainability features to meet AI Act and NIST expectations.
Therapists must retain ultimate decision-making authority to prevent erosion of the therapeutic alliance and ensure clinical accountability [ 2 ].

ONRAMP-AI-VRAR Step 4 requires clear delineation between AI-autonomous actions (e.g., modulating exposure length), human-mediated decisions (e.g., introducing trauma content), real-time dashboards for clinician review, and post-session logs for board oversight.
Early iterations should include robust human-in-the-loop structures, particularly for high-risk decisions [ 31 ].

Skills (Mandatory): conduct a layered/interactive consent walkthrough for XR/AI; explain limits of automation and where human-in-the-loop is required; document boundaries of AI autonomy in the care plan.

Collect patient-reported outcomes, system logs, biometric trends, and clinician feedback Flag discrepancies between AI and clinician recommendations for human review Update protocols based on new evidence, adverse events, bias detection, and evolving cultural concerns

ONRAMP-AI-VRAR incorporates Biometric Bias Audit Checklists to test subgroup performance, synthetic demographic simulations to evaluate disparity risk, and transparent fairness metrics and documentation pipelines.
Conducting quarterly reviews of equity impacts, content updates, and data safety audits

Rotating advisors may include cultural anthropologists, child and adolescent mental health specialists, disability rights experts, and AI fairness and transparency researchers to broaden involved stakeholders [ 1 , 26 ].

Using ONRAMP-AI-VRAR’s Data Flow Mapping Template, systems must ensure encryption, anonymization, access controls and comply with HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA if U.S.-based, or EU MDR/AI Act if international.
Oversight boards should review storage protocols, access logs, and data retention policies regularly.
AI systems should also include customizable settings to honor patient preferences and allow individuals to opt out or modify their therapeutic exposure during care [ 2 , 23 ].
Re-score quarterly and after material changes; escalate tier if risk, autonomy, scale, or sensitivity rises,
Rate harms by likelihood and impact, with categories for simulation sickness, re-traumatization, privacy breaches, etc.

unlisted_practices: Use layered, interactive consent procedures, such as VR walkthroughs and progressive disclosures, for AI-enabled immersive therapy.
Conduct periodic re-consent after significant system updates.
Define exposure intensity ceilings, stop-rules, and patient-controlled pause/exit controls for immersive therapy.
Screen patients for psychological risk before immersive therapy sessions and require human validation for high-risk patients.
Apply a cultural sensitivity rubric to immersive content, with review by diverse professionals and advocates.
Assign oversight tier using an objective governance tier score based on risk, data sensitivity, scale, phase, autonomy, competency, and resources.
Verify clinician competency in consent, cultural safety, data governance, and AI bias interpretation, with recertification after material system changes.
Design accessible, low-bandwidth, mobile-first deployment and audit demographics during performance reviews to reduce access inequities.
Have multiple licensed professionals review session content and datasets in early-stage systems to detect bias or emergent risks.

screen.reason: The paper introduces an operational protocol and governance framework (ONRAMP-AI-VRAR) for identifying, mitigating, and governing ethical risks in AI-driven immersive psychotherapy based on a targeted literature review.
